summary: Iteration 19 QA PT-PT — all 12 requested scenarios validated against LIVE OpenAI-backed webchat endpoint. Created /app/backend/tests/test_iter19_qa_ptpt.py (17 pytest cases across 12 test classes). Result: 17/17 PASSED in 64.85s. Regression run on iter 14/15/16/18 also GREEN (44/44 passed).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew past ~2660 lines — consider splitting webchat endpoints, admin agents endpoints and public endpoints into their own routers to keep review surface manageable.

guardrails.enforce_scheduling_link uses regex list to detect scheduler-like URLs; the '/marcar' and '/agendar' fallbacks are broad and could nuke legitimate marketing links on other agent tenants — currently safe because it always substitutes with scheduling_link, but consider scoping the substitution to non-whitelisted hosts only.
memory.collect_facts has grown into a mixed responsibility (facts + conversation flags + PT variant hints) — consider splitting `collect_facts` vs `collect_flags` to improve testability.
test_credentials: Not required — used public webchat endpoint (no auth). Admin creds if needed: admin@consenso-agents.com / 100%Consenso
seed_data_creation: None. Conversations created with TEST_iter19_* external_user_id prefixes for easy identification; auto-created via webchat, not manually seeded.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_iter19_qa_ptpt.py covers all 12 QA scenarios (sticky lang EN/FR, PT variant question + no-reask, obrigado-intent reclassify, Maria Consenso Plus description, gender-neutral Clara+Maria, Clara SEO recognition, Maria users-count no-reask after 'eu' x2, Maria quote flow asks name first, Clara Pipedrive link, Maria consenso-shop link, Clara real-estate isolation, Clara chatbot redirect to Plus, Clara no Calendly invention, URL whitelist for both agents). Tests are tolerant (marker-based) since LLM output varies. Total runtime ~65s. All previous iter18 guardrails still pass. External_user_ids use TEST_iter19_* prefix; if cleanup needed, filter conversations collection by that prefix.
rca of the issue: No bugs found. Guardrails (scrub_repeated_questions, ensure_pt_variant_question, apply_gender_neutral, enforce_scheduling_link, filter_urls_by_whitelist, ensure_scheduling_link) + memory.collect_facts flags (scheduling_confirmed, ask_pt_variant, language_variant) + _sticky_language (short-msg fallback to prev lang) all behave as designed. The determinism of the guardrail bundle is what makes the LLM-backed tests pass reliably despite prompt-model variance.
